question: Got Eternal Life?
answer: Eternal life is a gift from God through Jesus Christ. We've all sinned and deserve punishment, but Jesus, who was without sin, died on the cross to take that punishment for us. By trusting in Jesus and believing He rose from the dead, we can receive forgiveness and the promise of eternal life. It's not about what we do, but about trusting in what Jesus already did. If you want to accept this gift, simply express your faith and gratitude to God for His grace and forgiveness.

question: Got Forgiveness?
answer: Forgiveness is like wiping the slate clean, an act of love and grace that doesn't depend on whether we deserve it. We all need God's forgiveness because we've all sinned, which separates us from Him. Thankfully, Jesus took the punishment for our sins on the cross, offering us forgiveness and eternal life. To receive it, all you have to do is trust in Jesus and ask God to forgive you. It's not something you can earn—it's a gift from God, freely given through His love for us.

question: I am a Muslim. Why should I consider becoming a Christian?
answer: As a Muslim, you might wonder why consider Christianity. The heart of Christian belief lies in Jesus' claim that He is the way to God, as shared in John 14:6. Christians believe that Jesus lived a sinless life, died for our sins, and rose again, offering a path to eternal life. The Bible teaches that we can't earn our way to heaven through good deeds but can be saved through faith in Jesus, who bore our sins on the cross. Exploring the Bible may help you understand these beliefs more deeply, and it's about seeking a personal relationship with Jesus, trusting in His grace and love for you. If this resonates, you might express your faith through a prayer to God, acknowledging your sins and accepting Jesus as your Savior. Remember, it's a personal journey, and God is with you in your search for truth.

question: What are the four spiritual laws?
answer: The Four Spiritual Laws are a simple way to understand the Gospel message. First, God loves you and has a wonderful plan for your life. However, our sin separates us from God, and we can't experience His plan without His help. Thankfully, Jesus is God's solution for our sin—He died and rose again to restore our relationship with God. Finally, to embrace this gift of salvation, we need to place our faith in Jesus as our Savior. If you're ready to trust in Him, you can express your faith through prayer, thanking God for His grace and the gift of eternal life.

question: How do I get right with God?
answer: To get right with God, it's important to first acknowledge our sin and turn away from it. We all fall short, but God loves us so much that He sent Jesus to save us. By confessing our sins, believing in Jesus' death and resurrection, and trusting Him as our Savior, we can be forgiven and have a renewed relationship with God. Like the prodigal son who returned to his loving father, God welcomes us with open arms when we come back to Him. A simple prayer expressing your faith and gratitude is a great start, but it’s your trust in Jesus that truly brings salvation.

question: How can I know for sure that I will go to heaven when I die?
answer: To be sure of going to heaven, God wants us to know that it is all about trusting in Jesus. The Bible tells us that if we believe in Jesus, we have eternal life (1 John 5:13). Our sins separate us from God, but Jesus' sacrifice on the cross opened the way to forgiveness and eternal life as a free gift. It's not about what we do, but about accepting Jesus' love and grace. If you're ready to trust Him, you can simply pray, acknowledging your sins and believing in Jesus' death and resurrection for salvation. It's a step of faith that brings peace and assurance of eternal life with Him.

question: Is Jesus the only way to heaven?
answer: Yes, Jesus is the only way to heaven. The Bible clearly teaches that salvation is only found through Him. Jesus Himself stated in John 14:6 that He is "the way, the truth, and the life," and no one can come to the Father except through Him. This is because Jesus was uniquely chosen by God, lived a perfect life, died for our sins, and rose again. Through faith in Jesus, we receive forgiveness and eternal life.

question: Is there life after death?
answer: Yes, there is life after death according to the Bible. When we die, our bodies return to the earth, but our spirits live on. For those who believe in Jesus Christ, this means eternal life in heaven. Jesus, who conquered death by rising again, assures us of this promise. However, the Bible also warns that those who reject Christ will face eternal separation from God in hell. The choice of our eternal destination is made in this life through faith in Jesus. Now is the time to accept this gift of life with God.

question: What does it mean to accept Jesus as your personal Savior?
answer: Accepting Jesus as your personal Savior means recognizing who He truly is—God in human form who came to teach, heal, and ultimately die for our sins. It's not just about attending church or doing good deeds; it's about having a personal relationship with Jesus where you trust His sacrifice as the payment for your sins and His resurrection as your hope for eternal life. By placing your faith in Jesus, you acknowledge that His death was the necessary sacrifice for your sins and that He offers forgiveness and eternal life. It's about saying, "I believe in You, Jesus, and accept You as my Savior."

question: What is the right religion for me?
answer: Choosing a religion isn't like choosing your favorite ice cream flavor. While there are many paths and voices calling for our attention, Christianity stands out because of Jesus Christ. Unlike other religious figures who remain in their graves, Jesus rose from the dead, proving His power over death and affirming His claim to be the only way to God. Jesus offers a true relationship with God, forgiveness, and the hope of eternal life. If you're seeking a meaningful connection with God and the assurance of His love and forgiveness, Jesus invites you to come to Him. Trusting Him is about more than a set of rules—it's about entering into a life-changing relationship with the living Savior.

question: What is the Romans Road to salvation?
answer: The Romans Road to salvation is a simple way to explain how to have a relationship with God, using verses from the book of Romans. It starts with recognizing that everyone has sinned (Romans 3:23) and understanding that the consequence of sin is death (Romans 6:23a). But God offers the gift of eternal life through Jesus, who died for our sins (Romans 6:23b, 5:8). To be saved, we need to confess that Jesus is Lord and believe in His resurrection (Romans 10:9, 10:13). Once we believe, we are justified and have peace with God, knowing nothing can separate us from His love (Romans 5:1, 8:1, 8:38-39). If you feel called to follow this path to salvation, you can pray in your own words, trusting Jesus for forgiveness and eternal life.

question: What is the sinner’s prayer?
answer: The sinner's prayer is a heartfelt prayer to God, acknowledging our sinfulness and our need for Jesus as our Savior. It's not about saying specific words but about truly understanding and believing that Jesus died and rose for us, taking the punishment we deserve. By placing our faith in Him, we receive forgiveness and the promise of eternal life. If you feel ready, you can pray something like, "God, I know I'm a sinner and need Your forgiveness. I trust in Jesus as my Savior. Thank you for saving me. Amen."

question: What is a Christian?
answer: A Christian is someone who follows Jesus, which means trusting in Him and His teachings. It's not just about going to church or being a good person; it's about having a personal relationship with Jesus, believing in His death and resurrection for our sins, and being renewed by His Spirit. This faith makes us part of God's family, marked by loving others and living according to God's Word.

question: What does it mean to be a born again Christian?
answer: Being a born again Christian means experiencing a spiritual transformation. Jesus explained to Nicodemus that to enter God's kingdom, one needs to be "born from above," emphasizing a renewal that only comes through faith in Christ. This rebirth signifies leaving behind our old selves and becoming new creations, forgiven and alive in God's Spirit. It's not about physical birth, but a heartfelt decision to trust in Jesus, accepting His love and grace, and becoming a child of God.

question: What is the way of salvation?
answer: If you're searching for something more in life, feeling lost, or wondering about your purpose, Jesus is the key to finding fulfillment and salvation. Jesus said He is the bread of life, the light of the world, and the good shepherd, meaning He can satisfy your spiritual hunger, brighten your path, and offer genuine care. Our separation from God due to sin creates a void only Jesus can fill. By believing in Jesus and trusting in His sacrifice for our sins, we can receive forgiveness and eternal life. Jesus died and rose again out of love, so that we might have a relationship with God and live eternally with Him. If this touches your heart, consider taking a step of faith and trust in Him today.

question: How can I become a Christian?
answer: Becoming a Christian is all about having a personal relationship with Jesus. It starts with understanding that we all have sinned and need salvation, which Jesus offers by dying on the cross to take the punishment for our sins. To become a Christian, simply trust in Jesus as your Savior, believing that His sacrifice was sufficient for you. It's not about rituals or traditions, but about faith in Jesus and accepting His love and grace.

question: How can I become a child of God?
answer: To become a child of God, you need to have faith in Jesus Christ. This means recognizing that Jesus is God's Son, who lived a perfect life and died on the cross to pay for our sins. By believing in Him and turning away from sin, you receive new life and become part of God’s family. It's not about doing good deeds on your own but embracing Jesus' love and grace. As God's child, you grow to love and follow Him more each day, knowing you'll be with Him forever.

question: How do I convert to Christianity?
answer: Converting to Christianity is about starting a personal relationship with Jesus, believing that He is the Son of God who died for your sins and rose again. It's recognizing your need for salvation, turning away from sin, and trusting in Jesus alone to save you. This transformation is not just about changing religions but about receiving God's gift of grace and beginning a spiritual journey with Jesus that brings forgiveness and eternal life. If you're feeling drawn to this path, you can express your faith through prayer, thanking God for His grace and trusting in Jesus as your Savior.

question: What are the steps to salvation?
answer: Salvation isn't about following a list of steps or completing a checklist. The core message is simple: believe in Jesus Christ as your Savior. It's about recognizing that Jesus has already done all the necessary work for us through His life, death, and resurrection. We just need to have faith in Him, trusting Him alone for our salvation. All the other practices, like baptism and good deeds, are results of being saved, not requirements to earn it.

question: What is true religion?
answer: True religion isn’t just about following rules or performing rituals; it’s about having a genuine relationship with God. While many religions try to bridge the gap between humanity and God through strict practices, true religion, as shown in Christianity, recognizes that God has already bridged this gap through Jesus. Instead of earning salvation through actions, Christians believe that it is a gift from God. The rules and rituals in true religion are expressions of gratitude and love because of what Jesus has done, not a means to earn His favor.

question: How can I not go to hell?
answer: To avoid going to hell, the key is to accept Jesus Christ as your Savior. The Bible explains that we've all sinned, and sin separates us from God, deserving of an eternal penalty. But God, in His love, sent Jesus to pay that penalty on the cross, and His sacrifice is the path to salvation. Simply trust in Jesus, believe He died for your sins, and accept Him into your heart. God promises that faith in Jesus will save you from hell because He doesn’t want anyone to go there.

question: Going to heaven—how can I guarantee my eternal destination?
answer: To be sure you're going to heaven, the Bible teaches that faith in Jesus Christ is the key. Jesus Himself said He is the way, the truth, and the life, and no one comes to the Father except through Him. This means acknowledging Jesus as the Savior who died for our sins and rose again is crucial. It's not about earning our way there, but trusting in His sacrifice and accepting Him as Lord. Remember, it's a personal decision to believe and follow Jesus, and that faith assures us of eternal life with God.

question: What does it mean that Jesus saves?
answer: "Jesus saves" means that Jesus, who is God in human form, came to Earth to rescue us from the separation our sins create between us and God. Our sins deserve eternal separation from God, but Jesus paid for our sins by dying on the cross and rising again, offering us a way to be united with God. This salvation is a gift that we receive through faith, by trusting in Jesus alone for forgiveness and eternal life. If you believe this and want to accept Jesus as your Savior, you can pray and express your trust in Him, asking for His help to live a life of gratitude and purpose.

question: How can I be saved?
answer: Being saved is about securing your eternal destiny, and it's the most important decision you can make. We all need salvation because sin separates us from God and leads to eternal destruction. God provided a way for us through Jesus Christ, who died and rose again to pay for our sins. To be saved, simply believe in Jesus and trust Him as your Savior. It's a gift from God—just accept it with faith.

question: Who can be saved?
answer: Anyone can be saved through faith in Jesus. As John 3:16 tells us, God loves the world so much that He offers eternal life to anyone who believes in His Son. It’s not about what we do or our past mistakes; it’s about accepting God’s grace, which is a gift we receive by believing in Jesus. No one is beyond God’s reach—He saved people from all kinds of backgrounds in the Bible, showing us that His love and mercy are for everyone. If you feel moved to accept Jesus today, you can simply pray, expressing your faith in Him and asking for forgiveness and new life.

question: Where do you go when you die?
answer: When we die, the Bible tells us we have two destinations: heaven or hell. Our sins separate us from God, but through Jesus, who lived and died for us, we can be forgiven and receive eternal life in heaven. It’s through faith in Jesus and accepting His sacrifice that we find salvation. God offers us this choice; if we choose to trust in Jesus as our Savior, heaven awaits us.

question: What is the plan of salvation?
answer: The plan of salvation is God's way of rescuing us from the consequences of sin, which separates us from Him. We all need saving because we've all sinned, but God, in His love, provided a solution through Jesus Christ. Jesus lived a perfect life, died for our sins, and rose again, offering us salvation. To be saved, we simply need to believe in Jesus, trusting Him fully as our Savior. It's about turning away from sin and embracing the love and forgiveness God offers through His Son. If you're ready to accept this gift, place your faith in Jesus and receive His promise of eternal life.

question: I have just put my faith in Jesus...now what?
answer:
Congratulations on your new journey with Jesus! To help you grow in your faith, here are a few steps you can take: 

First, understand that you are saved through Jesus’ sacrifice, and nothing can separate you from God's love. Find a Bible-believing church where you can connect with others, learn more about God's Word, and worship together. Make time daily for prayer and reading the Bible to strengthen your relationship with God. Surround yourself with supportive friends who can help you grow spiritually, and consider being baptized as a public declaration of your faith. Enjoy this beautiful new chapter in your life!

question: Is God real?
answer: God's existence is evident through three main ways: creation, His Word, and His Son, Jesus Christ. When we look around at the intricate design of the world and the universe, it points to a Great Designer. Our innate sense of morality and longing for something greater suggests that God has placed eternity in our hearts. The Bible speaks of God as a self-evident truth, and Jesus' life, death, and resurrection offer powerful testimony to His reality. Ultimately, belief in God is a step of faith, supported by the evidence all around us.

question: Who is Jesus Christ?
answer: Jesus Christ is more than just a great teacher or prophet; according to the Bible, He is God in human form. Jesus Himself claimed to be God, as seen in passages like John 10:30 and John 8:58, where He equates Himself with God. The Bible presents Jesus as essential for our salvation because only God could provide the perfect sacrifice to pay for the sins of the world. Accepting who Jesus is matters because, as C.S. Lewis pointed out, if His claims were false, He would not be a good moral teacher but rather a deceptive figure. However, if true, He is our Savior, the only way to God.

question: Is Jesus God?
answer: Yes, Jesus is God. While He never used those exact words, Jesus made claims that showed His divinity. For example, in John 10:30, He said, "I and the Father are one," leading others to accuse Him of claiming to be God. Jesus’ followers also affirmed His deity. Verses like John 1:1-14 and Acts 20:28 speak of Jesus as God in the flesh, and He accepted worship, which only God deserves. Moreover, Jesus’ divine nature is crucial for salvation because only God could fully pay for our sins. So, Jesus is God, both in what He said and in what His followers and the Bible reveal about Him.

question: If I convert to Christianity, I will be persecuted. Should I follow Jesus?
answer: Choosing to follow Jesus is a significant decision that often comes with challenges, including potential persecution. Jesus teaches that being His disciple means being willing to give up earthly comforts, even when it’s tough. Many believers throughout history have faced suffering but found strength and joy in Jesus’ presence and the promise of eternal life. While the road may be hard, the love and eternal rewards offered through knowing Christ far outweigh the temporary struggles. Consider what truly matters to you and where you find your ultimate hope and security.

question: What are the attributes of God?
answer: God is truly amazing, and understanding His attributes helps us know Him better. The Bible teaches us that God is eternal, all-powerful, and all-knowing, always present everywhere, and unchanging, which makes Him utterly reliable. He's holy, just, and righteous, but also full of grace and love, seeking a personal relationship with each of us. God is our Creator, the Most High, perfectly sovereign, and a Trinity, meaning He is three in one. While we can't fully comprehend Him, His Word reveals enough to guide us in worship and grow in love with Him.

question: What is Christianity and what do Christians believe?
answer: Christianity is all about having a personal relationship with God through Jesus Christ. Christians believe that Jesus died for our sins, was buried, and rose again, offering salvation to anyone who has faith in Him. It's not about following a list of rules, but about trusting in Jesus’s sacrifice on the cross to restore our broken relationship with God. Christians also rely on the Bible as God's inspired Word and believe in one God in three persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Salvation is a gift from God, and through it, believers can live in victory over sin, guided by the Holy Spirit.

question: Is the Bible truly God’s Word?
answer: Yes, the Bible is truly God's Word. It's unique because it's a unified story written over 1,500 years by diverse authors, yet it all holds together without contradiction. The Bible includes detailed prophecies, especially about Jesus, that have come true, confirming its divine origin. Its power is evident in the countless lives it has transformed. Historically, its accuracy is proven by archaeology, and despite attacks over centuries, it endures. The sincerity and integrity of its authors, who were willing to die for the truth they shared, also testify to its divine inspiration. Ultimately, it's God's way of revealing Himself and His love to us.

question: What is the meaning of life?
answer: The meaning of life is about finding fulfillment and purpose through a relationship with God, which is made possible through Jesus Christ. Many people chase after achievements, wealth, or pleasure, only to find a sense of emptiness. The Bible tells us that true meaning comes from glorifying God and living in a way that reflects His image. Jesus offers us a full life, free from aimless wandering, by inviting us to follow Him and experience the joy of living for something greater than ourselves.

question: Do Christians have to obey the Old Testament law?
answer: Christians are not required to follow the Old Testament law because it was given specifically to the nation of Israel. When Jesus died on the cross, He fulfilled and ended the Old Testament law, and now Christians are guided by the law of Christ, which is to love God with all our heart and to love our neighbors as ourselves. This doesn't mean the Old Testament law is irrelevant; it can still guide us in understanding how to love God and others. But, as followers of Christ, our focus is on His command to love, which naturally leads us to live in ways that honor God and care for others.

question: Is the deity of Christ biblical?
answer: Yes, the deity of Christ is indeed biblical. Jesus and His followers clearly claimed and demonstrated that He is God. The Bible shows this in many ways: Jesus forgave sins, performed miracles, and was worshiped as God. His resurrection, witnessed and preached by His disciples, confirms His divine nature, as only God could conquer death. The transformation of His followers and the birth of the Church further support this truth.

question: Is salvation by faith alone, or by faith plus works?
answer: Salvation, according to the Bible, is by faith alone, not by faith plus works. Ephesians 2:8-9 makes it clear that we are saved by grace through faith, a gift from God, not by our own efforts. While James 2:24 might seem to suggest we need works too, it's actually emphasizing that true faith naturally results in good deeds. These works show our faith to the world, but they are not what saves us. Salvation is through Jesus’ work on the cross, and our faith in Him leads us to live lives full of good works as evidence of our genuine faith.

question: Who is the Holy Spirit?
answer: The Holy Spirit is not just a mystical force or an impersonal power; He is God and a divine person with a mind, emotions, and will. The Bible describes the Holy Spirit as being present everywhere and all-knowing, confirming His divinity. Scriptures like Acts 5:3-4 and Psalm 139 highlight that lying to the Holy Spirit is lying to God, and that His presence is everywhere. The Holy Spirit can think, feel, and make decisions, acting as our Comforter and Counselor, just as Jesus promised.

question: How can I know God’s will for my life?
answer: To know God's will for your life, it starts with repenting of sin and trusting in Christ, as that's His foundational desire. Once you accept Jesus, God wants to guide you through His Word and desires for you to live a life that includes gratitude, good works, and avoiding things like immorality. While God doesn’t always reveal everything at once, He leads us step by step, and as we align our lives with His ways, we begin to understand His will more clearly. Walking closely with God, through prayer and obedience, helps us tune into His desires for us, much like knowing a friend well enough to guess what they'll say. If our hearts are in the right place, God will place His desires in them, guiding us naturally. Remember, it's about wanting what He wants, trusting that He will lead you in the right direction.

question: How can I overcome sin in my Christian life?
answer: Overcoming sin in your Christian life is a journey where God provides several resources to help. First, rely on the Holy Spirit by choosing to follow His guidance over your own desires. This involves daily walking with Him and letting His influence grow in your life. Second, immerse yourself in the Bible, as it equips you and reveals areas for growth, helping you stay on the right path. Third, make prayer a priority, as it connects you with God's strength and guidance. Finally, lean on your church community for support and accountability, as having others by your side can encourage you and keep you accountable. Remember, progress may be slow or quick, but God is faithful to help you grow.

question: Why should I not commit suicide?
answer: I'm so sorry to hear you're feeling this way, and my heart goes out to you. Please know that you are not alone in this, and there is hope. God loves you deeply, and He wants to guide you through this dark time into His light. Jesus, who understands rejection and suffering, offers forgiveness and hope. He can restore your broken heart and bring joy back into your life. If you're considering suicide, please seek help immediately by calling a hotline or reaching out to someone close by. Remember, you are precious, and there is a path to healing and hope through Jesus.

question: What happens after death?
answer: In Christian belief, after death, believers in Jesus are said to go immediately to be with Him in heaven, while their bodies remain until they are resurrected and glorified. For those who don't believe, they go to a temporary place of torment, awaiting final judgment. Eventually, everyone will be resurrected, and believers will enjoy eternal life with God, while unbelievers face eternal separation from Him. Essentially, what happens after death depends on one's relationship with Jesus.

question: Eternal security - is it biblical?
answer: Eternal security, or the belief that once we are saved, we are always saved, is indeed biblical. The Bible assures us that God's power keeps us secure in our salvation; it's not something we have to maintain ourselves. Verses like John 10:28-29 remind us that Jesus and the Father hold us firmly in their hands, and nothing can separate us from God's love, as stated in Romans 8:38-39. Our eternal life is a promise sealed by the Holy Spirit, so we can trust that God will hold us until the end.

question: What does the Bible say about suicide?
answer: Suicide is a deeply tragic reality, but the Bible offers hope and assurance in Jesus. Many biblical figures, like Solomon, Elijah, Jonah, and Paul, experienced deep despair, yet found renewed strength and purpose by turning to God. The Bible assures us that God knows our struggles and offers comfort through His presence and the support of fellow believers. While suicide is a sin, it doesn't determine one's eternal destiny; salvation rests in God's grace through faith in Christ. If you're struggling with suicidal thoughts, please reach out for help immediately through hotlines or local support. Remember, you are not alone, and God is ready to offer His comfort and hope.

question: Is once saved, always saved biblical?
answer: Yes, the idea that "once saved, always saved" is biblical. When you accept Christ, you're brought into a relationship with God that secures your salvation eternally. This is because salvation is an act of God, where He gives us a new heart and spirit, and nothing can separate us from His love. Scriptures like Romans 8:38-39 assure us that once we are saved, our salvation is secure forever.

question: Do Christians and Muslims worship the same God?
answer: While Christians and Muslims both believe in one true God who created the universe, there's a significant difference in how each faith understands God. Christians believe in the Trinity, where God is one being in three Persons: the Father, the Son (Jesus Christ), and the Holy Spirit. This belief is central to Christianity because it includes Jesus's incarnation, death, and resurrection, offering salvation from sin. Muslims do not share this concept of the Trinity or the role of Jesus as the Son of God, leading to fundamental differences in understanding who God is. So, while both faiths worship one God, their views on His nature are distinct.

question: What does the Bible teach about the Trinity?
answer: The Trinity is a foundational Christian belief that God exists as one God in three distinct persons: the Father, the Son (Jesus), and the Holy Spirit. Each is fully God, yet there is only one God, not three. This can be hard to grasp because our human minds can't fully comprehend the infinite nature of God. The Bible supports this concept, but it's important to remember that it’s a mystery that points to the greatness of God. Rather than get tangled in trying to fully understand it, we can focus on the wonder and majesty of God's nature.

question: What does the Bible say about drinking alcohol?
answer: The Bible doesn't prohibit drinking alcohol, but it does caution against drunkenness and becoming mastered by it. Drinking in moderation is seen as permissible, and even Jesus drank wine, which was common in biblical times due to water contamination. However, it's important for Christians to avoid excess and consider their influence on others. While alcohol itself isn't sinful, drunkenness and addiction are. It's often wise for Christians to abstain, especially if it might lead others astray or become a personal struggle.

question: What does the Bible say about Christian tithing?
answer: Tithing in the Bible originally comes from the Old Testament, where Israelites gave 10% of their crops and livestock. In the New Testament, however, Christians are not commanded to follow a strict tithing system. Instead, giving is encouraged as an act of worship and should be done according to one's ability and with a joyful heart. It’s about being generous according to what you can manage and supporting the needs of the church community. Pray for guidance and remember that God loves a cheerful giver.

question: What does the Bible say about divorce and remarriage?
answer: The Bible emphasizes that God deeply values marriage and does not favor divorce, as seen in Malachi 2:16. However, He acknowledges that divorce does happen because humans are imperfect. Generally, the Bible discourages remarriage after divorce, but there are exceptions, like when an unbelieving spouse leaves or when there's sexual immorality involved. It's also essential to remember that reconciliation and forgiveness can restore a marriage, even after serious issues. While some may find biblical support for divorce in cases of desertion or infidelity, it's important to seek God's guidance and be open to forgiveness and healing. God’s love remains constant, even for those who have experienced divorce or remarriage.

question: What is the importance of Christian baptism?
answer: Baptism is important because Jesus commanded it as a way for believers to publicly profess their faith and discipleship. It's a beautiful symbol of our identification with Christ's death, burial, and resurrection, showing that we have died to sin and now live a new life in Him. While it’s not required for salvation, baptism is an act of obedience that illustrates the inward change in a believer’s life. A believer should seek to be baptized soon after coming to faith to express their commitment to following Jesus.

question: What are the Ten Commandments?
answer: The Ten Commandments are a set of ten important guidelines God gave to Israel after their exodus from Egypt. They can be found in Exodus 20 and Deuteronomy 5, and they cover our relationship with God and with others. They remind us not to worship other gods or idols, to treat God’s name with respect, to rest on the Sabbath, and to honor our parents. They also teach us not to murder, commit adultery, steal, lie, or covet. These commandments show that we can't perfectly keep them, highlighting our need for God’s mercy and grace through Jesus.

question: Who was Cain’s wife?
answer: The Bible doesn't specifically name Cain's wife, but it's most likely that she was a close relative like a sister or niece. Since Adam and Eve were the first humans, their children would have had to marry each other. In those early days, genetic defects were not a concern because Adam and Eve were created perfectly and their immediate descendants were healthy. It wasn't until later, when there were more people, that God set boundaries against inter-family marriages. Cain's fear for his life after killing Abel suggests there were already many people around, possibly siblings or even nieces and nephews.

question: What does the Bible say about sex before marriage?
answer: The Bible views sex as a beautiful gift meant to be enjoyed within the bounds of marriage. It teaches that sex before marriage, often referred to as fornication, falls under sexual immorality, which God warns against. Verses like 1 Corinthians 7:2 and Hebrews 13:4 emphasize keeping sexual relations within marriage to honor God and maintain purity. This approach not only aligns with God’s design for marriage and family but also helps prevent issues like unwanted pregnancies and broken family structures. By waiting until marriage, we honor God’s plan and protect the sanctity of this special bond.

question: What does the Bible say about women pastors?
answer: The Bible's stance on women pastors is a topic of significant debate. In passages like 1 Timothy 2:11-14, the apostle Paul indicates that women should not hold positions of spiritual teaching authority over men, which has been interpreted to mean that women should not serve as pastors. This teaching is based on the order of creation and the roles assigned by God, not on the capabilities or worth of women. Women have many vital roles and gifts within the church, such as teaching other women and children and contributing to various ministries, but according to this interpretation, pastoring men is not one of them.

question: What does the Bible say about homosexuality?
answer: The Bible describes homosexual activity as a sin but draws a distinction between behavior and inclination. Being tempted is not a sin; it's acting on those temptations that the Bible talks about. We all have struggles and weaknesses, but with God's help, we're called to resist sin and live according to God's design. Importantly, no sin is greater than God's grace, and forgiveness is available to everyone, regardless of past actions, through Jesus Christ. So, while the conversation around this is complex and can be challenging, the key is to trust in God's love and strength to guide us.

question: What does the Bible say about interracial marriage?
answer: The Bible doesn't oppose interracial marriage; rather, its guidance focuses on spiritual unity. In the Old Testament, God instructed the Israelites not to marry those who worshipped false gods, and in the New Testament, Christians are reminded not to be unequally yoked with unbelievers. The key concern is faith in Christ, not skin color or ethnicity. Interracial marriage can beautifully reflect our unity in Christ. Couples should be prepared for possible challenges due to prejudice, but above all, their love and faith should guide their relationship.

question: Did God create evil?
answer: It might seem that if God created everything, He must have created evil too. But evil isn't a "thing" like a physical object; it's more like the absence of good, just as darkness is the absence of light. God allowed for the possibility of evil because He gave us and angels the freedom to choose. Without the possibility of choosing something other than good, our love and service to God wouldn't be genuine. So, while God didn't create evil, He allowed it so we could have true free will and not be like robots, forced to follow Him without choice. It's a complex topic, and some aspects are beyond our full understanding, but God's ways are always holy and perfect.

question: Why is God so different in the Old Testament than He is in the New Testament?
answer: There's a common misconception that God seems different between the Old and New Testaments, but the truth is, God is consistently loving and just throughout both. In the Old Testament, we see God's compassion and mercy as He guides His people, much like a loving father. The New Testament reveals God’s love more fully through Jesus, who came to offer eternal life. Both Testaments show God's unwavering nature—He is the same loving, merciful, and just God, always desiring a relationship with His people.

question: What does it mean that God is love?
answer: When we say "God is love," it means that love is at the very heart of who God is. The Bible describes love as patient, kind, selfless, and forgiving, and God embodies all these qualities perfectly. Jesus demonstrated this love through His life and sacrifice, showing kindness to everyone and putting others before Himself. God's greatest expression of love is sending Jesus to offer us eternal life, even when we didn't deserve it. This love is pure and in harmony with all of God's other qualities, like justice and holiness. When we accept Jesus, we are invited to experience and share this incredible love through the Holy Spirit.

question: Does God still speak to us today?
answer: Yes, God still speaks to us today, though not always in the audible way we might expect. Primarily, He communicates through the Bible, which contains all we need for salvation and living a godly life. God can also guide us through our circumstances, our conscience, and the inner transformation of our minds. While it’s possible for God to speak audibly, it is rare, and any message we hear should align with what the Bible teaches.

question: Who created God?
answer: The question "Who created God?" can be a bit misleading because it assumes God is like everything else that needs a cause. But God is different—He's uncaused and uncreated. He simply exists. If nothing existed, then nothing could ever come into being. But since things do exist, something must have always existed, and that's what we call God. He's the eternal Creator who started everything.

question: What does it mean to have the fear of God?
answer: Having the fear of God means having a deep respect and reverence for Him. For believers, it's not about being scared of God, but rather understanding His holiness and righteousness, which leads us to live in a way that honors Him. It involves respecting Him, obeying Him, and being in awe of His greatness. This reverential fear guides us to wisdom and encourages us to walk in His ways, love Him, and serve Him with all our hearts.

question: Is God male or female?
answer: God isn't limited to human gender as He is a spiritual being without physical form. In the Bible, God reveals Himself using masculine titles and pronouns, like "Father," to help us understand Him better. Both men and women are created in God's image, which speaks to our spiritual and moral capacity, not physical traits. While God chose to communicate through a masculine form, this doesn't mean He is male in a human sense—it's just a way for us to relate to Him within our understanding.

question: Does God still perform miracles?
answer: Yes, God still performs miracles today, but they might not be as dramatic or obvious as those recorded in the Bible. The miracles we see now are often overlooked or dismissed, yet they're still a part of God's work in the world. It's important to remember that the biggest miracle of all is Jesus coming to save us, as that's the foundation of our faith. While miracles in the past served to confirm the truth of Jesus and the apostles, we now have the Scriptures to guide our faith. So, rather than seeking more miracles, we should focus on the profound miracle of salvation through faith in Jesus Christ.

question: Is God / the Bible sexist?
answer: The Bible isn't sexist, but it does describe a time when society was patriarchal, reflecting the cultural norms of that era. However, this doesn't mean God endorses those actions. The Bible shows the consequences of sin, like sexism, but also offers a solution through Jesus. In Christ, we're all equal—there's no difference in worth between men and women at the cross. The Bible assigns different roles, not as a sign of inequality, but as a way of maintaining order. Understanding Scripture reveals that true equality comes from a relationship with God, where every person is equally valued and loved.

question: Does God hear / answer the prayers of a sinner / unbeliever?
answer: God does hear and sometimes answer the prayers of unbelievers, though not in the same way as those who follow Him. While some believe that God only hears a sinner's prayer for salvation, the Bible shows instances where God responded to unbelievers' prayers, such as in the stories of Nineveh, Hagar, and others. God's responses can come from His compassion or when prayers align with His will. Ultimately, God promises that those who truly seek Him will find Him, and He is gracious in His interactions with all people.

question: Why is God a jealous God?
answer: When the Bible describes God as a "jealous God," it means He deeply desires our worship and devotion because they rightfully belong to Him. Unlike human jealousy, which often involves wanting what others have, God's jealousy is about protecting what is His—our love and worship. It's similar to how a husband might feel protective if someone else tried to claim his wife's affection. God’s jealousy is a reminder that He alone is worthy of our wholehearted devotion.

question: Can monotheism be proven?
answer: Monotheism—the belief in one true God—is supported by various arguments. Biblically, Scripture consistently declares the existence of one God, as seen in verses like Deuteronomy 6:4 and 1 Timothy 2:5. Historically, many cultures show evidence of starting with monotheism before drifting into polytheism. Philosophically, it's argued that the universe's order and God's perfection point to a single, all-powerful deity. While these arguments may not convince everyone, they provide a strong foundation for those open to exploring them further.

question: Is it wrong to question God?
answer: It's not wrong to question God, but it's important to approach Him with an honest and open heart. Throughout the Bible, many people, including prophets and disciples, asked God questions from a place of humility and genuine seeking. God welcomes sincere questions, as they show a desire to understand and trust Him more deeply. However, questioning with a rebellious or untrusting heart is discouraged, as it stems from unbelief. Remember, God knows our hearts and intentions, and He invites us to seek Him with faith and humility.

question: Has anyone ever seen God?
answer: No one has seen God in His full, glorious form because He is spirit, and our physical eyes can't perceive Him that way. However, Jesus, who is both God and man, reveals God to us. When people saw Jesus, they were essentially seeing God in human form. There are instances in the Bible where individuals have encountered manifestations of God, known as theophanies, like when Moses or Jacob had experiences with God. These were not direct views of God's full glory but rather ways God chose to reveal Himself to them. To truly know and see God, we look to Jesus, who makes the Father known to us.

question: Does God change His mind?
answer: God doesn't change in His character or plans like we do, but He interacts with us based on our actions. When we see stories where it seems like God changes His mind, it's usually because people have changed, like when Nineveh repented and God showed mercy instead of judgment. God's nature is constant; He always responds to righteousness with forgiveness and to unrepentance with judgment. This shows His unchanging love and justice, not a change in His essence.

question: Is it wrong to be angry with God?
answer: It's natural to feel angry with God during tough times, but it's important to remember that God is in control and His plans are always perfect, even if we can't see it. Being angry with God can stem from a lack of trust in His sovereignty, and while He understands our feelings, it's not right to hold onto that anger. Instead, we should bring our emotions to Him in prayer, trusting that He is working for our good and will bring us peace and strength. Life will have its challenges, but by trusting God and growing in faith, we can navigate those difficulties and be a source of comfort to others.

question: Is there a conclusive argument for the existence of God?
answer: The existence of God is a topic that has been debated for centuries, with many arguing both for and against it. But when we ask, "Why is there something rather than nothing?" we find that reality being an illusion or self-created doesn't hold up. We're left with two possibilities: an eternal universe or an eternal Creator. Science and philosophy suggest the universe had a beginning, implying it can't be eternal, pointing instead to an eternal Creator. Furthermore, examining the nature of this Creator aligns perfectly with the God of the Bible. While atheism struggles to provide sufficient evidence against God's existence, belief in God not only stands as a reasonable position but also offers a path of salvation through Jesus Christ.

question: Is it wrong to feel disappointment with God?
answer: Feeling disappointed with God is a part of being human and not necessarily wrong. It often happens when our expectations don't align with God's actions. However, God operates according to His perfect will, which might not always make sense to us, but is ultimately for our good. By aligning our wills with His and trusting in His plan, we can find peace and contentment, knowing that He works all things for our benefit and His glory.

question: How should I understand the concept of the Father God?
answer: Understanding God as our Father is about recognizing the incredible love He has for us. The Bible tells us that God has "lavished" His love upon us, making us His children through Jesus. This means right now, at this very moment, we are part of His family, enjoying all the rights and privileges that come with it. As our heavenly Father, God cares for us, provides for us, and even disciplines us like a loving parent, so we can grow closer to Him and share in His holiness. More than anything, being called God's children is a profound honor and a testament to His boundless love.

question: What does it mean that God is eternal?
answer: When we say God is eternal, we mean He has no beginning or end—He's always been and always will be. The Bible simply starts with, "In the beginning God…," showing that God was already there before time began. This eternal nature is seen in God's self-description to Moses as "I AM," which implies His constant presence across all time. Jesus also affirmed His eternal nature by saying, "Before Abraham was born, I AM." Creation itself points to God’s eternality, as it follows His timeless plan. Those who trust in Christ will share in this eternity with God.

question: Is God fair?
answer: God is indeed fair, but His fairness is not always what we might expect. If fairness meant everyone got exactly what they deserved, we would all be facing eternal separation from God because of our sin. Thankfully, God is also merciful and sent Jesus to take the punishment we deserved, offering us a chance at salvation through faith. While some struggle with the idea of being chosen by God, the Bible teaches that anyone who truly seeks Him will find Him. God's ways may seem mysterious, but He is just, loving, and offers grace to all who believe.

question: Does God punish us when we sin?
answer: God doesn't punish us for our sins in terms of condemnation because Jesus already took care of that on the cross. Instead, as a loving parent, God disciplines us to guide us back onto the right path. This discipline helps us grow and become more like Christ. While we might face natural consequences for our actions, God's discipline is meant for our good, helping us to mature in our faith and live more according to His desires.

question: Does God tempt us to sin?
answer: God does not tempt us to sin. Instead, He may test us to strengthen our faith and character, much like He did with Abraham when asked to sacrifice Isaac. These tests are meant to prove our faith and help us grow, not to cause us to sin. Temptations to sin come from Satan, his forces, or our own desires, not from God.

question: Is it sometimes God’s will for believers to be sick?
answer: Yes, sometimes it is God's will for believers to be sick. While God is in control of everything, sickness is part of the fallen world we live in due to sin entering creation. God allows sickness for various purposes, like teaching us, disciplining us, or even revealing His power, as seen in the Bible. Even when we don't understand why we're suffering, we can trust that God is sovereign and that He can bring good out of every situation. In eternity, we'll have a clearer understanding, and perhaps the questions we have now won't even matter.

question: Where is God?
answer: God is everywhere, always with us. He reigns from heaven, yet His presence is everywhere throughout creation. When life is tough and we feel alone, it’s important to remember that God hasn’t abandoned us. Even in our deepest pain, God’s love surrounds us, and He promises never to leave us. Like a quilt-maker turning a mess of threads into something beautiful, God is working through all things for our good, even if we don’t see it right now. So when it’s hard to see what God is doing, trust His heart and His unchanging presence.

question: What does it mean that God is infinite?
answer: When we say God is infinite, we're saying that He has no limits. He knows everything (omniscient), He's all-powerful (omnipotent), and He's present everywhere (omnipresent). This means nothing surprises Him, nothing can stop Him, and there's nowhere we can go where He isn't with us. Even though God is far beyond our complete understanding, He has lovingly revealed Himself to us through creation, the Bible, and Jesus, so we can know Him and how to live in relationship with Him.

question: What does it mean that God is omnipotent?
answer: When we say God is omnipotent, it means He has all power over everything, everywhere, and at all times. This power is most clearly seen in His creation, where He spoke the universe into existence, and He continues to sustain it. God's omnipotence also extends to His control over earthly authorities and spiritual forces, showing nothing is beyond His command. While God can do anything that aligns with His holy nature, there are things He cannot do, like lie, because that would go against His perfection. Jesus, as God incarnate, displayed His omnipotence through miracles and the resurrection, showing His control over life and death. Amazingly, this mighty power is shared with believers, allowing us to experience His strength, especially in our times of weakness.

question: What does it mean that God is omnipresent?
answer: When we say God is omnipresent, we mean that He is everywhere at all times. He is not bound by space or time, so there's no corner of the universe where He's absent. Whether in joy or struggle, God is present with us, even when we don't see or feel Him. This also means God is aware of everything, from the smallest detail to the vastness of the cosmos. His presence can bring comfort and guidance, and it reminds us that we can always reach out to Him in prayer, no matter where we are.

question: What does it mean that God is omniscient?
answer: When we say God is omniscient, it means He knows everything—every detail, every thought, and every future event. This includes knowing our hearts, our experiences, and even things as small as a sparrow falling or a hair on our head. Jesus, even in His humanity, displayed this knowledge, knowing people's thoughts and lives before meeting them. However, He also chose to experience human limitations. Despite our sins, God's love for us is eternal, and we find comfort in knowing that nothing is too hard for Him. As we trust in Him, we are assured of His unfailing presence and care.

question: Why does God require faith?
answer: God requires faith because, just like any relationship, trust is essential. We can't fully know anyone, not even ourselves, and the same goes for our understanding of God. Even though God has shown us enough of Himself through creation, the Bible, and Jesus, our sinful hearts often struggle to trust. God invites us to trust Him by removing the barrier of sin through Jesus, allowing us to have a meaningful relationship with Him. Just like the Israelites who saw God's wonders but still doubted, faith remains a choice we are invited to make based on what God has revealed about Himself.

question: What is the difference between God’s sovereign will and God’s revealed will?
answer: God's sovereign will is like His grand plan that includes everything He decrees, whether directly or by allowing it. It's often hidden from us until it unfolds, like Joseph's journey to Egypt. On the other hand, God's revealed will is what He has clearly instructed us in the Bible—His precepts and commands, like acting justly and loving mercy. While we're called to obey His revealed will, sometimes we fall short, but we can always come back to His grace.

question: What does it mean that God is holy, holy, holy?
answer: When we say God is "holy, holy, holy," it highlights His supreme holiness. This phrase, repeated by heavenly creatures in both Isaiah and Revelation, emphasizes God's unique and perfect nature. God's holiness sets Him apart from everything else, filling us with awe and reverence. It's a reminder of His majesty, and while we can't be holy by ourselves, through Jesus, we can share in God's holiness. The threefold repetition also hints at the Trinity, acknowledging the holiness of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. This profound holiness shows that God is constant and unchanging in both the Old and New Testaments.

question: What is the key to truly knowing God?
answer: To truly know God, it's essential to understand what He has revealed about Himself in the Bible. This starts with recognizing our own sinfulness and the need for repentance, turning to Jesus, who is our Savior. By faith in Jesus, who shows us who God is, we find the path to knowing God. Engaging with the Bible, living out its teachings, committing to prayer, worship, and fellowship, and being open to the Holy Spirit's guidance are all ways to deepen this relationship with God. Through Jesus and the Holy Spirit, we experience God’s love and truly come to know Him.

question: What are the different names of God, and what do they mean?
answer: God is known by many names in the Bible, each highlighting a unique part of His character. For example, "El" and "Elohim" speak to His might and power, while "Yahweh" (or Jehovah) reveals His eternal presence and accessibility, as in "Yahweh-Jireh," meaning "The Lord Will Provide." There's "El Shaddai," meaning "God Almighty," emphasizing His ultimate power over all, and "Adonai," which signifies His lordship. Each name like "Yahweh-Shalom" (The Lord Our Peace) or "Yahweh-Rapha" (The Lord Who Heals) expresses how intimately God cares for and interacts with us, His people.

question: Who is God?
answer: God is the Supreme Being, the Creator and Ruler of everything, perfect in power, goodness, and wisdom. The Bible shows us God's nature and works, revealing that He is spirit and exists as the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. God is infinite, unchanging, all-knowing, and all-powerful. His character is just, loving, truthful, compassionate, merciful, and holy. Through Jesus, God came to us, offering forgiveness and salvation, making Jesus the bridge between God and humanity. To truly understand God, we look to Jesus and His life.

question: What is the biblical understanding of the wrath of God?
answer: The biblical understanding of God's wrath is that it's His holy and justified response to sin and disobedience. Unlike human anger, which can be flawed and unjust, God's wrath is always righteous. In the Old Testament, God's wrath often came as a response to idolatry and sin, but He also provided a way for people to turn away from it through repentance. The New Testament reinforces this, showing that God's wrath against sin was taken on by Jesus at the cross, offering eternal life to those who believe in Him. For Christians, living by the Spirit helps us avoid sinful anger and embrace peace. Ultimately, only through Jesus can we be assured that God's wrath won't fall on us.

question: Is it really true thatallthings are possible with God?
answer: Yes, with God, all things are possible, but that doesn't mean He will do anything that contradicts His holy nature or purposes. God’s power is limitless, but He won't act against His own character, like committing sin or performing illogical acts such as creating a stone He cannot lift. The Bible shows us that God can do amazing things that align with His will, like parting the Jordan River or granting a child to Elizabeth in her old age. Our understanding of what God can do should be guided by Scripture, which reveals His desires and promises.

question: Why did God command the genocide of the Canaanites?
answer: This is certainly a tough question, and it's important to approach it with sensitivity. In the Bible, God's command to the Israelites to destroy the Canaanites was not about indiscriminate violence. The Canaanites were known for their deeply immoral practices, and God had given them over 400 years to change their ways. When they didn't, judgment came through the Israelites. God wanted to protect His people from falling into idolatry and the harmful practices of the Canaanites, which is why He commanded their complete removal. The intention was also to prevent future conflicts and fulfill a longstanding prophecy. It's crucial to remember that God is sovereign and just, though His ways can be hard for us to understand. God desires repentance and life, not death, and those who turned to Him, like Rahab, were spared.

question: Does God know the future?
answer: Yes, God knows the future. The Bible accurately predicts events, such as Jesus being born in Bethlehem as foretold centuries earlier. This shows God’s complete understanding of past, present, and future. He is omniscient, meaning He knows everything, and we can trust that all His prophecies will come to pass in His perfect timing. God is truly the Alpha and Omega, the Beginning and the End.

question: Does God make mistakes?
answer: God doesn't make mistakes. He's perfect and knows everything, so nothing surprises Him. Even when we see stories where God seems to regret something, like in Genesis 6, it's more about His compassionate response to human choices, not an admission of error. In our lives, it might feel like things go wrong, but Romans 8:28 reminds us that God works all things for the good of those who love Him. We can trust that, whatever happens, God has a loving and wise purpose behind it all.

question: Is it wrong to be frustrated with God?
answer: It's normal to feel frustrated with God at times, but it's important to understand that this often comes from our own misunderstandings or lack of trust. Stories like Martha's and Jonah's show us how frustration can cloud our vision and that God has perfect timing and plans. Instead of letting frustration take over, we can find peace by trusting in God’s goodness, accepting His timing, and submitting to His will. When we feel overwhelmed, we can cast our frustrations on God because He truly cares for us.

question: Why does God demand, seek, or request that we worship Him?
answer: God doesn't seek our worship because He needs it; rather, it's for our benefit. He is the Creator and sustainer of all things and needs nothing from us. Instead, worship aligns our hearts with Him, the true source of love, light, and life. When we worship God, it sets our priorities straight, helping us to love Him and others rightly. It fills us with gratitude and leads to a purposeful life centered on His grace. If we don't worship God, we're likely to place that worth on something else, which can never truly fulfill us.

question: Why was God so evident in the Bible, and seems so hidden today?
answer: It may seem like God was more visible during Biblical times because He often used miracles and direct communication to guide and reveal His plans to people. Today, God has completed His revelation through Scripture, which means we may not witness those same miraculous events. However, God is still very present through His creation and speaks to us through the Bible and the Holy Spirit, who guides us and brings Scriptures to mind. Our journey now is about living by faith, trusting in what God has already done, and recognizing His work in our lives and the world, even when it seems hidden.

question: What is the immutability of God?
answer: The immutability of God means that God never changes. Scriptures like Malachi 3:6 and James 1:17 highlight that God is consistent—there is no alteration in His nature, promises, or character. Since God exists outside of time, He doesn't change as we do, because change implies imperfection or the need for growth, neither of which apply to Him. Even when the Bible talks about God "changing His mind," it's more about changes in human situations rather than any real change in God Himself. God is always perfect, always all-knowing, and always unchanging.

question: How do I get the image of God as imposing and angry out of my mind?
answer: To reshape your view of God from angry to loving, it's helpful to remember the simple truth: "God is love" (1 John 4:8). God's essence is pure love, and even His anger is filtered through this love. For those who believe in Jesus, God's anger was directed at the cross, and He no longer sees us as sinners but through the perfect lens of Jesus' sacrifice. If you still struggle with seeing God as angry, it might help to examine your relationship with Him. By seeking Him through prayer and scripture, you'll discover that He is a loving Father who yearns for a personal relationship with you.

question: What does it mean that God provides?
answer: God's provision is about so much more than just material things. Like a loving parent, He knows what we truly need and provides in ways that help us grow to be more like Christ. It's not about acquiring wealth, but about trusting God to care for our physical, spiritual, and emotional needs. He wants us to focus on eternal life and trust Him with our daily needs through a deep relationship with Him. We can find peace, comfort, and strength in His abundant love, knowing that He is always with us, guiding and providing for us in ways beyond what we can imagine.

question: Is God’s love conditional or unconditional?
answer: God's love is truly unconditional. He loves us not because of who we are or what we do, but because it's His nature to love. Despite our sins and shortcomings, God showed the ultimate act of love by sending Jesus to die for us. However, receiving His love fully means responding in faith to Jesus, which brings us into a special relationship with Him. God's unconditional love is available to all, but choosing to embrace it leads to a deeper, covenant relationship with Him.

question: Why does God allow good things to happen to bad people?
answer: It's natural to wonder why good things happen to bad people, just as we question why bad things happen to good people. In Psalm 73, Asaph struggled with this same issue until he realized, in God's presence, that the prosperity of the wicked is only temporary. Their apparent success is fleeting, like a dream, while true riches are found in a relationship with God, leading to eternal life. So, when life seems unfair, remember that our ultimate joy and fulfillment are in God, who offers us eternal riches through Jesus Christ.

question: What is the grace of God?
answer: The grace of God is His incredible kindness and favor towards us, even though we don't deserve it. It's like God choosing to bless us when our actions should have led to punishment. Through His grace, God offers us forgiveness, a relationship with Him, eternal life, and so much more, just because He loves us. It's His amazing gift that invites us into a beautiful relationship with Him, simply because He's gracious and loving.

question: What does it mean to honor God?
answer: Honoring God means showing Him the highest respect and valuing Him above all else. Just like the elders in heaven lay their crowns before God, we honor Him by reflecting His goodness and character in our lives through our words and actions. It's about demonstrating the love and goodness of God, much like Jesus did. This can be done by living purely, giving generously, and dedicating our lives to Him. True honor comes from the heart, not just outward actions, and involves delighting in God, seeking Him earnestly, and making choices that reflect His importance in our lives.

question: Is God a person?
answer: Yes, God is a person, but not in the sense of being human. When we say God is a person, we mean He has a mind, emotions, and a will. The Bible shows God as having personal characteristics through His actions and expressions, like love and compassion. He exists in three distinct Persons—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—each with their own mind, emotions, and will, yet all are fully God.

question: What does it mean to praise God?
answer: Praising God means expressing our love, gratitude, and admiration for Him. In the Bible, praising God is shown in many forms, like singing, giving thanks, and honoring Him for His power and greatness. The Psalms are full of beautiful examples of praise, calling us to praise God everywhere, with everything we have—from instruments to our own voices. Jesus was praised during His time on earth, and the early church also valued praising God together. Ultimately, praising God on earth prepares us for the eternal celebration of worship we’ll share in heaven.

question: What does it mean to be in the presence of God?
answer: Being in the presence of God means experiencing His closeness through the Holy Spirit within us, a promise for all who believe in Jesus. Although sin once separated us from God's physical presence, His Spirit reassures us of His continual presence. While we might not always *feel* His presence, especially during difficult times, God never truly leaves us. Our awareness of Him grows through faith, obedience, and the joy that comes from trusting Him, even in trials. This closeness leads to a deep joy, reminding us of the everlasting joy to come when we’ll be fully in His presence.

question: Why should I care if God exists?
answer: Caring about God's existence is important because it shapes the way we see the world and ourselves. If God exists, as Christians believe, then everything we do and the values we hold are grounded in His nature and teachings. This belief can guide us in addressing not only our spiritual needs but also in seeking justice and compassion in our world. Through faith in Jesus, God offers us love, forgiveness, and a deep connection, which can transform our lives now and eternally.

question: Why does God love us?
answer: God loves us not because we're lovable or deserving, but simply because His very nature is love. Although we often fall short and live in ways that oppose God, He still showers us with His love, which is sacrificial and unconditional. This is beautifully demonstrated through Jesus' sacrifice on the cross for our sins, showing that God's love is deeply personal and boundless. In essence, God loves us because He is love itself.

question: Why does God test us?
answer: God tests us to strengthen our faith and prove its genuineness, not because He needs to know, but to show us that our faith is real. Through tests and trials, He helps us grow spiritually, developing perseverance and maturity. Just like a tree digs its roots deeper during a storm, we should root ourselves in God's Word and promises. While tests can be challenging, God never gives us more than we can handle with His strength, and every trial is for our ultimate good and growth in faith.

question: Is God opposed to pleasure?
answer: No, God isn't opposed to pleasure. In fact, He created us to experience and enjoy it. God designed the world with beauty and gave us the ability to delight in it, whether through the taste of good food, the warmth of friendship, or the joy of celebrations. He is not against us enjoying life but warns us about pleasures that can lead us away from Him. Our ultimate joy is meant to be found in a relationship with God, where He offers us eternal pleasures. So, while it's great to enjoy the gifts God gives, they should never replace our connection with Him.

question: What does it mean that God is spirit?
answer: When we say "God is spirit," it means that God the Father isn't bound by a physical body and is invisible, as described in John 4:24. This allows Him to be everywhere at once, unlike a physical being. Although God doesn't have a body, we can still know Him personally and worship Him with our hearts and minds, beyond just physical rituals or locations. This concept helps us understand that God's essence is beyond human limitations, making Him infinitely present and alive in our lives.

question: What does it mean that God is light?
answer: When the Bible says "God is light," it's highlighting God's pure holiness and goodness, without any trace of sin. Light symbolizes truth, righteousness, and the revelation of hidden things, contrasting with darkness which represents sin and evil. As believers, we're called to walk in this light, growing in faith and becoming more like Jesus, who is the "light of the world." By reflecting His light, we help guide others from darkness to the truth of God's love and salvation.

question: Can God lie?
answer: God cannot lie because He is perfectly holy and truthful. His nature is pure, and everything He says and does reflects absolute truth. This means that we can completely trust God and His Word, the Bible, as flawless and reliable. Since God is unchanging and His promises are sure, we are called to emulate His truthfulness in our own lives. Just as Jesus, who is God, embodies truth, we are encouraged to speak and live truthfully.

question: Can God sin?
answer: God cannot sin because sinning would be completely against His nature. God is perfectly holy, righteous, and true, and these qualities are essential to who He is. If God were to sin, He would no longer be God, which is impossible. Despite being perfectly holy, God loves us deeply and sent His Son, Jesus, to redeem us from sin, bringing us closer to Him through His sacrifice.

question: How should a believer respond to the characteristics of God?
answer: As believers, we respond to God's incredible characteristics in a few profound ways. When we grasp God's holiness, it leads us to repentance and awe, recognizing our need for His grace and mercy. His immense love, revealed through Jesus, inspires us to humility, repentance, and love for others. God's sovereignty reminds us of His eternal power and majesty, encouraging us to submit to Him with trust and gratitude. Like the faithful figures in the Bible, we are moved to worship, obedience, and reverence when we encounter God's presence.

question: Did God create sin?
answer: God didn't create sin; He created everything perfectly good. Sin came into the world because of rebellion, not because God made it. Sin is anything that goes against God's perfect standard. God gave us free will, allowing us to choose between right and wrong. Although the potential for sin exists because of free will, God desires us to choose Him and experience the blessings of a righteous life. He does not delight in punishment but wants everyone to turn back to Him and find eternal joy.

question: Does God care about the little things that happen in our lives?
answer: Absolutely, God cares about the little things in our lives. Scripture tells us that God even knows the number of hairs on our heads, which shows His attention to detail. He values us deeply, more than the birds of the air, whom He also takes care of. Throughout Jesus' life, we see how He took time to meet people's needs and welcomed children, showing that no concern is too small for Him. So, trust that God is genuinely interested in every part of your life, no matter how minor it seems.

question: Does God get angry?
answer: Yes, God does get angry, but His anger is very different from ours. God's anger is always righteous and is directed towards wickedness and injustice, much like a loving parent who gets upset at anything that harms their child. In the Bible, we see God's anger when people stray from His ways or when they act unjustly, as He desires to protect His people and restore their relationship with Him. However, for those who accept Jesus, God's wrath for sin is satisfied through Jesus' sacrifice on the cross, offering us freedom and no condemnation in Him.

question: Does God hate?
answer: It's a complex idea, but God, who is love, can also hate. God hates sin and wickedness because they oppose His nature of love. The Bible shows that God loves the world deeply, even sacrificing His Son for it, but He must judge sin, which involves judging those who persist in sinful rebellion. His desire is for everyone to turn from sin and find refuge in Christ, receiving His perfect love and forgiveness. Despite His hatred for sin, God’s ultimate wish is for transformation and redemption through repentance.

question: Does God love me?
answer: Absolutely, God loves you deeply and personally! Despite knowing all our imperfections, God's love is unconditional and demonstrated throughout the Bible. From the beginning, He created us with intimate care, and even when our relationship with Him was broken, His love remained. The ultimate expression of this love is seen in Jesus Christ, who came to earth to redeem us. Through His sacrifice, God shows that nothing can separate us from His love. So, remember, God’s love for you is steadfast and true.

question: Why does God allow people to be disabled / handicapped?
answer: God allows disabilities as part of the brokenness of our world, which is a result of sin. However, He also uses these challenges to show His glory and strength. The Bible tells us that God can use anyone, regardless of their abilities, for His purposes and that His power is made perfect in weakness. In the end, disabilities are temporary, and a day will come when all will be healed. Until then, those who rely on God in their weakness are blessed with a special closeness to Him.

question: Is there anything God cannot do?
answer: God is all-powerful and wise, having created everything in the universe. There's nothing too hard for Him, and He can reach even those who seem far from salvation. However, God cannot act against His own nature—He cannot lie or sin because He is holy and just. His love is so great that He sent His Son, Jesus, to die for our sins, offering us forgiveness and eternal life through faith in Him. Even when we face challenges, God remains a present help, ready to guide us with His unwavering love and strength.

question: What does it mean that the Trinity is God in three Persons?
answer: When we say the Trinity is God in three Persons, we're talking about the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, each having their own distinct personality, intellect, emotion, and will. They are not human persons; instead, they represent three unique aspects of the one true God. Each has a unique role, like in creation and salvation, yet they are perfectly unified in their divine essence. This relationship within the Trinity also shows us how God's love is eternal, as each Person has always loved the others. It's a mystery that can be hard to grasp, but it's all about understanding God as one in essence, three in personhood.

question: What does it mean that God is good?
answer: When we say God is good, it means He is the ultimate standard of goodness, always acting in right, true, and loving ways. There is no evil in Him, and His intentions are always pure. Everything He creates and does reflects His goodness, and this goodness is evident in His plan for our redemption through Jesus. God's goodness invites us to trust Him and find joy and refuge in His love.

question: What does it mean that God is just?
answer: When we say God is just, we mean He is fair and righteous in all His ways. He sees everyone equally and rewards and punishes with perfect fairness, without showing favoritism. God’s justice ensures that wrongdoing is addressed, but He also made a way through Jesus for our sins to be forgiven, showing His deep love alongside His justice. The Lord wants us to reflect His character by acting justly, loving mercy, and walking humbly with Him.

question: What does it mean that God looks at the heart (1 Samuel 16:7)?
answer: In 1 Samuel 16:7, when God says He looks at the heart, it means God evaluates us based on our inner character and faithfulness, not just our outward appearance. While people often judge by what they see on the surface, God sees our true intentions and moral life. Like David, who might not have looked like a king, but had a heart aligned with God, our worth is seen by God in our faith and sincerity. This reminds us to nurture our inner lives and trust that God values who we truly are.

question: What is God’s relationship to time?
answer: God's relationship to time is quite different from ours. While we live within time's boundaries, God exists beyond it. He is eternal, meaning He has no beginning or end and is not limited by time. Though God created time and the universe, He remains present with us in every moment, able to respond to our needs and prayers. This timeless nature doesn't make God distant; rather, it means He sees all of history and the future at once and is with us in the here and now.

question: Why does God allow the innocent to suffer?
answer: It's a tough question because suffering, especially of the innocent, is deeply heartbreaking. The Bible shows us that suffering isn't always linked to personal sin. Even Jesus addressed this, explaining that sometimes suffering is there so God's works can be shown. Our world is flawed and full of sin, which means everyone experiences pain, but God promises to use even this suffering for a greater purpose. He draws us closer to Him, strengthens our faith, and helps us focus on the hope of eternal life.
